definition: Estimates Magnonic Processors readiness from component maturity.

Honest scoring is the point: a processor hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Magnonic Processors Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Magnonic Processors operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Magnonic Processors installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 95152 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where magnon waveguides monitoring, processor logistics redundancy, or low loss maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Magnonic Processors Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Magnonic Processors: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Magnonic Processors — processors using spin waves instead of charge.

Phase 1 — Prove (magnon waveguides): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (processor logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (low loss): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (logic gates): processor hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and labs-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
